# Every form and its source

The public forms of dmipy-analytic 3.0.0, module by module: what each one is (the first paragraph of its docstring), the source its docstring cites, and whether `dmipy_analytic.jax` holds its JAX twin. The docstrings carry the assumptions each form holds under and its parameters.

## The physical constants: `dmipy_analytic.constants`

The physical constants of the dmipy packages, defined once, in SI units: the proton gyromagnetic ratio ``GAMMA`` in rad/(s T), its value per cycle ``GAMMA_BAR`` in Hz/T, and the vacuum permeability ``MU0`` in N/A^2.

| constant | value |
|---|---|
| `GAMMA` | 267513000.0 |
| `GAMMA_BAR` | 42576016.2913422 |
| `MU0` | 1.2566370614359173e-06 |

## The real spherical-harmonic basis: `dmipy_analytic.harmonics`

The orthonormal real spherical-harmonic basis every spherical-harmonic coefficient of the dmipy packages is written in, its compact layout, and its rotation matrices.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `cart2sphere` | Spherical coordinates ``[r, theta, phi]`` of cartesian ``[x, y, z]``, one point ``(3,)`` or ``N`` points ``(N, 3)``: ``theta`` in ``[0, pi]`` the polar angle from ``z`` (0 at the origin), ``phi`` in ``[-pi, pi]`` the azimuth from ``x``, DIPY's convention. |  |  |
| `n_sh_coeffs` | Coefficients in the compact layout up to ``lmax`` (even orders only unless ``full``). |  |  |
| `sh_block` | Slice of the compact array holding order ``l`` (``m = -l..+l``). |  |  |
| `real_sh` | Orthonormal real spherical harmonics in the compact layout. |  |  |
| `wigner_blocks` | Per order ``l``, the ``(N, 2l+1, 2l+1)`` real rotation matrices ``M^l(R)`` of the harmonic basis. |  |  |

## Orientation distributions: `dmipy_analytic.orientation`

The Watson and Bingham orientation distributions in closed form: their normalisation and their exact coefficients in the real spherical-harmonic basis of `dmipy_analytic.harmonics`.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `watson_zonal_ratios` | Exact zonal harmonic ratios r_l = J_l(kappa) / J_0(kappa) for even l. |  |  |
| `watson_sh` | Exact Tournier real SH coefficients of a Watson ODF. |  |  |
| `bingham_normalization` | Partition function of ``exp(-k1 (n.e1)^2 - k2 (n.e2)^2)`` over the sphere. |  |  |
| `bingham_canonical_sh` | Coefficients of the Bingham whose pose axis is ``z`` and whose concentrations are about ``x`` and ``y``: the canonical frame, before any rotation. |  |  |
| `bingham_sh` | Coefficients of a Bingham with a stated frame: the canonical form rotated. |  |  |

## Gaussian diffusion: `dmipy_analytic.gaussian`

Gaussian diffusion: the signal of free diffusion (the ball), of the stick, the zeppelin and the full diffusion tensor under a b-value or a b-tensor, and their orientation (powder) averages.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `ball` | The attenuation of free isotropic Gaussian diffusion, ``exp(-b D)``. | Stejskal and Tanner (1965), J. Chem. Phys. 42:288, the attenuation of the echo ``exp(-gamma^2 G^2 delta^2 D (Delta - delta/3)) = exp(-b D)``. | ✓ |
| `stick` | The attenuation of Gaussian diffusion along one axis only (the stick, a cylinder of zero radius), ``exp(-b D (n . u)^2)``. | Behrens et al. (2003), Magn. Reson. Med. 50:1077, the anisotropic compartment with ``d_perp = 0``. | ✓ |
| `stick_squared_cosine` | The attenuation of the stick at a given squared cosine of the angle between the gradient and its axis, ``exp(-b D cos^2(theta))``. |  | ✓ |
| `stick_btensor` | The attenuation of the stick under a b-tensor, ``exp(-D u^T B u)``. | Behrens et al. (2003), Magn. Reson. Med. 50:1077, with the b-matrix attenuation of Basser et al. (1994), Biophys. J. 66:259. | ✓ |
| `zeppelin` | The attenuation of an axially symmetric Gaussian tensor (the zeppelin) under a pulsed gradient, ``exp(-b (D_par (n . u)^2 + D_perp \|n_perp\|^2))`` with ``\|n_perp\|^2 = \|n\|^2 - (n . u)^2``. | Panagiotaki et al. (2012), NeuroImage 59:2241, the zeppelin (Gaussian anisotropic) compartment; Basser et al. (1994), Biophys. J. 66:259. | ✓ |
| `zeppelin_squared_cosines` | The attenuation of the zeppelin at given squared components of the gradient direction along and perpendicular to its axis, ``exp(-b (D_par cos2 + D_perp sin2))``. |  | ✓ |
| `zeppelin_btensor` | The attenuation of the zeppelin under a b-tensor, ``exp(-(D_perp tr B + (D_par - D_perp) u^T B u))``. | Basser et al. (1994), Biophys. J. 66:259; Westin CF et al. (2016), NeuroImage 135:345-362 (the b-tensor attenuation). | ✓ |
| `tensor` | The attenuation of a general Gaussian diffusion tensor under a pulsed gradient, ``exp(-b n^T D n)``. | Basser et al. (1994), Biophys. J. 66:259, with ``B = b n n^T``. | ✓ |
| `tensor_btensor` | The attenuation of a general Gaussian diffusion tensor under a b-tensor, ``exp(-sum_ij B_ij D_ij)``. | Basser et al. (1994), Biophys. J. 66:259: the attenuation is the exponential of minus the b-matrix contracted with ``D``. | ✓ |
| `time_dependent_diffusivity` | The apparent perpendicular diffusivity of a pulsed-gradient measurement in a medium with one-dimensional structural disorder, ``D_inf + A (ln(Delta/delta) + 3/2) / (Delta - delta/3)``. | Burcaw LM, Fieremans E, Novikov DS (2015), NeuroImage 114:18-37, the pulsed-gradient diffusivity (the ``ln(t)/t`` law integrated over rectangular pulses). | ✓ |
| `temporal_zeppelin` | The attenuation of the zeppelin whose perpendicular diffusivity is time dependent, ``exp(-b (D_perp + (D_par - D_perp)(n . u)^2))`` with ``D_perp =`` `time_dependent_diffusivity`. | Burcaw et al. (2015), NeuroImage 114:18; the compartment of Novikov DS et al. (2019), NMR Biomed. 32:e3998. | ✓ |
| `stick_powder_average` | The orientation average of the stick's attenuation over all axis directions, ``sqrt(pi) erf(sqrt(b D)) / (2 sqrt(b D))``; ``1`` at ``b = 0``. | Kaden et al. (2016), NeuroImage 139:346, Eq. 7 (the stick's spherical mean). | ✓ |
| `zeppelin_powder_average` | The orientation average of the zeppelin's attenuation over all axis directions, ``exp(-b D_perp) J_0(kappa) / 2`` with ``kappa = -b (D_par - D_perp)`` and ``J_0(kappa) = int_{-1}^{1} exp(kappa t^2) dt``. | Kaden et al. (2016), NeuroImage 139:346, Eq. 8 (the zeppelin's spherical mean). | ✓ |

## Restriction: the plane: `dmipy_analytic.restricted.plane`

Diffusion between two parallel impermeable plates in closed form: the short-gradient-pulse limit and the Gaussian-phase approximation of the signal along the plates' normal.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `sgp_long_time` | The signal between two plates in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a diffusion time long enough for the spins to explore the whole gap, ``2 (1 - cos(2 pi q d)) / (2 pi q d)^2``; one at ``q = 0``. | Balinov B, Jonsson B, Linse P, Soderman O (1993), J. Magn. Reson. A 104:17-25, Eq. 6. | ✓ |
| `sgp` | The signal between two plates in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a finite diffusion time ``tau`` (Callaghan's series): the diffraction pattern of the slit plus the modes of the gap, each decaying as ``exp(-xi^2 D tau / a^2)``, ``a = d/2``, with ``xi = n pi`` (the cosine modes about the midplane) and ``xi = n pi + pi/2`` (the sine modes); one at ``q = 0``. | Callaghan PT (1995), J. Magn. Reson. A 113:53-59 (the planar pore). | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase` | The signal between two plates of a pulsed gradient in the Gaussian-phase approximation, ``exp(-gamma^2 G^2 sum_{k odd} (8 d^2 / (k pi)^4) I_k)`` with the bracket of the Gaussian phase of a pair of rectangular pulses ``I_k = (2 lambda_k delta - 2 + 2 e^{-lambda_k delta} + 2 e^{-lambda_k Delta} - e^{-lambda_k (Delta - delta)} - e^{-lambda_k (Delta + delta)}) / lambda_k^2`` and the decay rates ``lambda_k = D (k pi / d)^2``. | the Gaussian phase approximation of Murday JS, Cotts RM (1968), J. Chem. Phys. 48:4938, applied to the planar pore; Balinov et al. (1993), J. Magn. Reson. A 104:17. | ✓ |

## Restriction: the cylinder: `dmipy_analytic.restricted.cylinder`

Diffusion inside an impermeable cylinder in closed form: the short-gradient-pulse limit and the Gaussian-phase approximation of the signal perpendicular to the axis, combined with free diffusion along it.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `sgp_long_time` | The signal across a cylinder in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a diffusion time long enough for the spins to explore the whole cross-section, ``(2 J_1(2 pi q R) / (2 pi q R))^2`` with ``R = d/2``; one at ``q = 0``. | Soderman O, Jonsson B (1995), J. Magn. Reson. A 117:94-97, Eq. 6. | ✓ |
| `sgp` | The signal across a cylinder in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a finite diffusion time ``tau`` (Callaghan's series): the diffraction pattern plus the radial and angular modes of the disk, each decaying as ``exp(-alpha^2 D tau / R^2)``; one at ``q = 0``. | Callaghan PT (1995), J. Magn. Reson. A 113:53-59 (the cylindrical pore); Neuman CH (1974), J. Chem. Phys. 60:4508. | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase` | The signal across a cylinder of a pulsed gradient in the Gaussian-phase approximation, ``exp(-2 gamma^2 G^2 sum_k (2 a_k D delta - 2 + 2 e^{-a_k D delta} + 2 e^{-a_k D Delta} - e^{-a_k D (Delta - delta)} - e^{-a_k D (Delta + delta)}) / (D^2 alpha_k^6 (R^2 alpha_k^2 - 1)))`` with ``alpha_k = mu_k / R``, ``a_k = alpha_k^2`` and ``mu_k`` the roots of ``J_1'``. | Van Gelderen P, DesPres D, van Zijl PCM, Moonen CTW (1994), J. Magn. Reson. B 103:255-260; the Gaussian phase approximation of Neuman (1974), J. Chem. Phys. 60:4508. | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase_waveform` | The signal across a cylinder of a sampled gradient waveform in the Gaussian-phase approximation, ``exp(-(gamma^2/2) sum_k B_k int int G(t) G(t') exp(-a_k D \|t - t'\|) dt dt')`` with ``B_k = 2 (R/mu_k)^2 / (mu_k^2 - 1)``, ``a_k = (mu_k/R)^2`` and ``mu_k`` the roots of ``J_1'``. | Stepisnik J (1981), Physica B+C 104:350-364 (the Gaussian-phase signal of an arbitrary waveform); Xu J et al. (2009), J. Magn. Reson. 200:189-197, Eq. 3. | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase_cosine` | The signal across a cylinder of a cosine gradient ``G cos(omega t)`` on ``[0, sigma]`` in the Gaussian-phase approximation, in closed form: the double integral of `gaussian_phase_waveform` for the cosine. | Stepisnik (1981), Physica B+C 104:350; Ianus A, Siow B, Drobnjak I, Zhang H, Alexander DC (2013), J. Magn. Reson. 237:128-136 (the oscillating-gradient Gaussian phase of a cylinder). | ✓ |
| `geometry_factor` | The geometry factor of the fast-eigenmode Gaussian-phase signal, ``gamma^2 sum_k B_k / alpha_k`` with ``B_k = 2 (R/mu_k)^2 / (mu_k^2 - 1)`` and ``alpha_k = (mu_k/R)^2 D``, s^3/(kg^2 m) in SI units. |  | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase_gamma_lm` | The signal of a cylinder of axis ``u`` for any gradient waveform in the fast-eigenmode Gaussian-phase limit, ``exp(-(phi_perp + phi_par))`` with ``phi_perp = C (2/3 int \|G\|^2 dt - (8 pi/15) sum_m Gamma_2m Y_2m(u))``, ``C =`` `geometry_factor` and ``phi_par = b_par D_par``. | the Gaussian phase of Stepisnik (1981), Physica B+C 104:350 for the cylinder's eigenmodes, expanded in the order-two harmonics of the encoding. | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase_exponent_coefficients` | The coefficients ``(c_0, c_2m)`` of the cylinder's perpendicular Gaussian-phase exponent in the harmonics of the axis direction, ``phi_perp(u) = c_0 + sum_m c_2m Y_2m(u)``, with ``c_0 = C (2/3) int \|G\|^2 dt`` and ``c_2m = -C (8 pi/15) Gamma_2m``. |  | ✓ |
| `capped_sgp_long_time` | The signal of a capped cylinder in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a long diffusion time: the cylinder across (`sgp_long_time`) times a pair of plates ``length`` apart along the axis (`dmipy_analytic.restricted.plane.sgp_long_time`). | Soderman and Jonsson (1995), J. Magn. Reson. A 117:94 for the cross-section; Balinov et al. (1993), J. Magn. Reson. A 104:17, Eq. 6 along it. | ✓ |
| `capped_sgp` | The signal of a capped cylinder in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a finite diffusion time ``tau``: the cylinder across (`sgp`) times a pair of plates ``length`` apart along the axis (`dmipy_analytic.restricted.plane.sgp`), both with the diffusivity ``diffusivity``. | Callaghan (1995), J. Magn. Reson. A 113:53 (the planar pore along the axis, the cylindrical pore across). | ✓ |

## Restriction: the sphere: `dmipy_analytic.restricted.sphere`

Diffusion inside an impermeable sphere in closed form: the short-gradient-pulse limit and the Gaussian-phase approximation of the signal.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `sgp_long_time` | The signal inside a sphere in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a diffusion time long enough for the spins to explore the whole sphere, ``(3 (sin x / x - cos x) / x^2)^2`` with ``x = 2 pi q R``, ``R = d/2``; one at ``q = 0``. | Balinov B, Jonsson B, Linse P, Soderman O (1993), J. Magn. Reson. A 104:17-25. | ✓ |
| `sgp` | The signal inside a sphere in the short-gradient-pulse limit at a finite diffusion time ``tau`` (Callaghan's series): ``E = F(x)^2 + 6 sum_{n,k: alpha_nk > 0} (2n + 1) alpha_nk^2 / (alpha_nk^2 - n(n+1)) [x j_n'(x) / (x^2 - alpha_nk^2)]^2 exp(-alpha_nk^2 D tau / R^2)`` with ``x = 2 pi q R``, ``R = d/2``, ``F(x) = 3 (sin x - x cos x) / x^3`` the uniform-sphere structure factor (the ground state, the long-time limit), ``alpha_nk`` the roots of ``j_n'`` and ``j_n`` the spherical Bessel function; one at ``q = 0``. | Callaghan PT (1995), J. Magn. Reson. A 113:53-59 (the spherical pore); Grebenkov DS (2007), Rev. Mod. Phys. 79:1077 for the eigenfunctions. |  |
| `gaussian_phase` | The signal inside a sphere of a pulsed gradient in the Gaussian-phase approximation, ``exp(-2 gamma^2 G^2 / D sum_k alpha_k^-4 / (R^2 alpha_k^2 - 2) (2 delta - (2 + e^{-a_k D (Delta - delta)} - 2 e^{-a_k D delta} - 2 e^{-a_k D Delta} + e^{-a_k D (Delta + delta)}) / (a_k D)))`` with ``alpha_k = x_k / R``, ``a_k = alpha_k^2`` and ``x_k`` the roots of ``j_1'``. | Murday JS, Cotts RM (1968), J. Chem. Phys. 48:4938-4945 (the sphere); Balinov et al. (1993), J. Magn. Reson. A 104:17. | ✓ |
| `gaussian_phase_waveform` | The signal inside a sphere of a sampled gradient waveform in the Gaussian-phase approximation, ``exp(-(gamma^2/2) sum_k B_k int int G(t) . G(t') exp(-a_k D \|t - t'\|) dt dt')`` with ``B_k = 2 (R/x_k)^2 / (x_k^2 - 2)``, ``a_k = (x_k/R)^2`` and ``x_k`` the roots of ``j_1'``. | Stepisnik J (1981), Physica B+C 104:350; Xu J et al. (2009), J. Magn. Reson. 200:189-197, Eq. 3 (the sphere); Murday and Cotts (1968), J. Chem. Phys. 48:4938. | ✓ |

## Restriction: the eigenmode (matrix) method: `dmipy_analytic.restricted.matrix_method`

The eigenmode (matrix) solution of restricted diffusion in a planar, cylindrical or spherical pore under a generalised gradient waveform -- Callaghan's 1997 matrix formalism (J. Magn. Reson. 129:74-84), extended to these three pores by Codd & Callaghan 1999 (J. Magn. Reson. 137:358-372, doi:10.1006/jmre.1998.1679), and restated by Barzykin 1999 (J. Magn. Reson. 139:342-353) and Grebenkov's review (Rev. Mod. Phys. 79:1077-1137, 2007).

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `cylinder_neumann_roots` | The first ``n_roots`` non-negative roots of ``J_m'(x) = 0``; ``m = 0`` includes the constant mode at 0: the Neumann eigenvalues of the unit disk, ``lambda = x^2`` for the mode ``J_m(x r) cos(m theta)``. ``n_roots`` is at least 1; for ``m = 0`` one root is the constant mode alone. |  |  |
| `sphere_neumann_roots` | The first ``n_roots`` non-negative roots of ``j_l'(x) = 0``; ``l = 0`` includes the constant mode at 0: the Neumann eigenvalues of the unit ball, ``lambda = x^2`` for the mode ``j_l(x r) P_l(cos theta)``. Bracketed on a grid of 40,000 points and refined by Brent's method. ``n_roots`` is at least 1; for ``l = 0`` one root is the constant mode alone. |  |  |
| `MatrixPore` | The closed form of one pore: ``MatrixPore(shape, size_m, D).signal(g, dt)``. |  | ✓ |
| `matrix_restricted_signal` | The restricted signal's magnitude for a single projected 1-D gradient schedule (T/m) at step ``dt`` (s), diffusivity ``D`` (m^2/s) and pore ``size_m`` -- the functional entry point for a caller that wants a number rather than `MatrixPore`'s object API. |  | ✓ |
| `matrix_restricted_batch` | ``matrix_restricted_signal`` over a stack of projected 1-D schedules ``g_axes`` (n_meas, n_t) sharing one ``dt``, ``D`` and ``size_m`` -- one `MatrixPore` (one unit-mode cache hit, one eigendecomposition scaled once) evaluated per measurement rather than rebuilt per call. |  | ✓ |

## Exchange: `dmipy_analytic.exchange`

Diffusion with exchange between compartments: the Karger model of exchanging Gaussian pools and its propagators under spin-echo and stimulated-echo encoding, and the forms of diffusion through permeable membranes.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `diffusion_time` | The effective diffusion time of a pulsed-gradient measurement, ``Delta - delta/3``. | Stejskal EO, Tanner JE (1965), J. Chem. Phys. 42:288 (the factor ``Delta - delta/3`` of the attenuation). | ✓ |
| `karger` | The Karger signal of two exchanging Gaussian pools, ``sigma_+ exp(-lambda_+) + (1 - sigma_+) exp(-lambda_-)`` with ``lambda_+/-`` the eigenvalues of the exchange-weighted dephasing matrix. | Karger et al. (1988), Adv. Magn. Reson. 12:1; Jelescu et al. (2022), NeuroImage 256:119277, Eqs. 3-5. | ✓ |
| `exchange_matrix` | The exchange generator of two pools in detailed balance, ``[[-kappa, k_ee], [kappa, -k_ee]]`` with ``k_ee = kappa f / (1 - f)``. | Karger et al. (1988), Adv. Magn. Reson. 12:1. | ✓ |
| `spin_echo_signal` | The signal of exchanging pools at a spin echo of finite radiofrequency pulses: the magnetisation summed over the pools after ``P_fp2 P_180 P_fp1 P_exc M0``, each ``P = expm(.)`` the propagator of one interval. | the multi-interval solution of the exchange-coupled Bloch-Torrey equation; Karger et al. (1988), Adv. Magn. Reson. 12:1 for the exchange generator. | ✓ |
| `stimulated_echo_signal` | The signal of exchanging pools at a stimulated echo of finite radiofrequency pulses, including the factor one half of the stimulated pathway: ``P_enc2 P_rec P_mix P_store P_enc1 P_exc M0``. | the multi-interval solution of the exchange-coupled Bloch-Torrey equation; Karger et al. (1988), Adv. Magn. Reson. 12:1. | ✓ |

## Relaxation and magnetization transfer: `dmipy_analytic.relaxation`

Relaxation and the exchange of magnetization between a free and a bound pool, in closed form.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `forward_rate` | Forward (free->bound) exchange rate k_f = kappa_MT * (S/V), s^-1. |  |  |
| `backward_rate` | Backward (bound->free) exchange rate k_r = 1/dwell_time, s^-1. |  |  |
| `bound_fraction` | Equilibrium bound-pool fraction f_b = k_f / (k_f + k_r). |  |  |
| `kappa_MT_from_forward_rate` | Invert k_f = kappa_MT * (S/V) -> kappa_MT (m/s). |  |  |
| `dwell_time_from_fraction` | Dwell time for a target equilibrium bound fraction at forward rate k_f. |  |  |
| `two_pool_generator` | Build the 7x7 generator A of the two-pool Bloch--McConnell system. |  |  |
| `evolve_two_pool` | Evolve the augmented state ``state0`` (7,) by time ``t`` under generator A: ``expm(A t) state0``. |  |  |
| `bloch_mcconnell_transverse` | Free-pool transverse magnitude \|Mxy,a\|(t) after a 90 on both pools (no RF). |  |  |
| `bloch_mcconnell_longitudinal` | Free-pool longitudinal Mza(t) under exchange (no RF, no transverse). |  |  |
| `mt_z_spectrum` | Steady-ish Z-spectrum: free-pool Mz after a CW saturation pulse vs offset. |  |  |
| `transverse_decay` | The transverse relaxation of the magnetisation over the time it is transverse, ``exp(-tau / T2)``. | Bloch F (1946), Phys. Rev. 70:460 (the transverse decay); Hahn EL (1950), Phys. Rev. 80:580 (the spin echo). | ✓ |
| `longitudinal_decay` | The longitudinal relaxation of the magnetisation stored along the field, ``exp(-tau / T1)``. | Bloch F (1946), Phys. Rev. 70:460 (the longitudinal component); Hahn EL (1950), Phys. Rev. 80:580 (the stimulated echo). | ✓ |
| `surface_to_volume` | The surface-to-volume ratio of a pore of the given size, 1/m: ``6/d`` for a sphere of diameter ``d``, ``4/d`` for an infinite cylinder, ``2/d`` for two plates a distance ``d`` apart. |  | ✓ |
| `surface_relaxation` | The relaxation at the walls of a pore in the fast-diffusion regime, ``exp(-rho (S/V) tau)``. | Brownstein KS, Tarr CE (1979), Phys. Rev. A 19:2446 (the fast-diffusion limit). | ✓ |
| `surface_relaxation_gamma_cylinders` | The surface relaxation of an ensemble of cylinders with a Gamma distribution of diameters, ``E_d[exp(-rho (4/d) tau)] = 2 (beta c)^(a/2) K_a(2 sqrt(beta c)) / Gamma(a)`` with ``c = 4 rho tau``, ``beta = 1/scale`` and ``a = shape + 2`` (the water of a cylinder scales with its cross-section ``d^2``). | Gradshteyn IS, Ryzhik IM, *Table of Integrals, Series, and Products*, 3.471.9; Brownstein and Tarr (1979), Phys. Rev. A 19:2446. | ✓ |
| `surface_relaxation_gamma_spheres` | The surface relaxation of an ensemble of spheres with a Gamma distribution of diameters, ``E_d[exp(-rho (6/d) tau)]``: `surface_relaxation_gamma_cylinders` with ``c = 6 rho tau`` and ``a = shape + 3`` (the water of a sphere scales with ``d^3``). | Gradshteyn and Ryzhik, 3.471.9; Brownstein and Tarr (1979), Phys. Rev. A 19:2446. | ✓ |
| `exterior_surface_to_volume` | The ratio of the cells' outer surface to the volume of the space around them, 1/m, ``k f / ((1 - f)(shape + m - 1) scale)`` for cells with a Gamma distribution of outer diameters. |  | ✓ |

## Extended phase graphs: `dmipy_analytic.epg`

Extended phase graphs: the coherence pathways of a schedule of RF pulses and gradient windings, and their amplitudes.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `Pulse` | An instantaneous RF pulse on the coherence lattice: its flip and its B1 phase, in degrees. |  |  |
| `Winding` | A free-precession interval: the gradient winds every transverse coherence by ``dk`` orders. |  |  |
| `Schedule` | A sequence as an ordered timeline of `Pulse` and `Winding` events. |  |  |
| `Pathway` | One branch that reaches coherence order zero at a readout: its amplitude and its history. |  |  |
| `enumerate_pathways` | Every pathway of ``schedule`` that reaches coherence order zero at a readout. |  |  |
| `splice_schedule` | A SPLICE train: the split acquisition of fast spin-echo signals (Schick 1997). |  |  |
| `cpmg_schedule` | A CPMG train: an excitation, then ``n_echoes`` refocusing pulses each between two unit windings. |  |  |
| `ste_schedule` | A three-pulse stimulated echo: excite, dephase, store, mix, recall, rephase, read. |  |  |
| `ste_amplitude` | The stimulated echo's amplitude: ``0.5 sin(a1) sin(a2) sin(a3)``, as the pathway product gives it. |  |  |
| `rf_operator` | The 3x3 mixing a pulse applies to ``(F+, F-, Z)`` at every coherence order (Weigel 2015, eq. 2.4). |  |  |
| `EPGState` | The configuration states of a spin ensemble: ``F`` over coherence orders ``-N..N`` and ``Z`` over ``0..N``. |  |  |
| `split_by_gate` | Propagate through ``events``, splitting the state whenever the gradient is ON. |  |  |
| `train_weights` | ``{gate: [amplitude at each readout]}``: what each microscopic gate contributes to each echo. |  |  |

## The fields of simple shapes: `dmipy_analytic.fields`

The magnetic fields of simple shapes in closed form: the field basis of a hollow cylinder of isotropic and anisotropic susceptibility (the myelin sheath), infinite and as a finite segment, and the field of a straight current segment.

| form | what it is | source | JAX |
|---|---|---|:---:|
| `hollow_cylinder_basis` | The 12 basis channels of one infinite hollow cylinder at points given by ``rho_vec`` ``(..., 3)``, the vector from the axis to the point (perpendicular to the axis), ``u`` ``(..., 3)`` the unit axis, ``a`` and ``b`` ``(...)`` the inner and outer radii (metres). Returns ``(..., 12)``: ``iso_local`` (``m / 3``), the five stored components of ``M_P`` (``zz`` follows from its trace), the six of ``M_A``; float64, broadcast over leading axes. |  | ✓ |
| `segment_basis` | The 12 channels of one FINITE segment of the hollow cylinder, seen from outside the sheath: the dipole kernel ``D = (I - 3 n n^T) / (4 pi r^3)`` integrated in closed form along the segment, whose ends are at axial coordinates ``z1 < z2`` from the point's foot on the axis (``c(z') = foot + z' u``, ``p - c = rho_vec - z' u``), times the sheath's cross-section ``A = pi (b^2 - a^2)``: ``M_P = A L``, ``M_A = -A sym(L T)`` with ``L`` the integrated tensor and ``T = P / 2 - I / 3`` the annulus-averaged director tensor. For an infinite line it is the outside formula of `hollow_cylinder_basis` (``M_P = -A S / 2 pi rho^2``, ``M_A = A S / 12 pi rho^2``), far away the point dipole of the segment's moment, ``A L (I - 3 r r^T) / 4 pi r^3``; a line cut into segments sums to the line exactly. Within the sheath's radius ``rho`` is continued at the surface (``rho >= b``): the value a point inside another segment's extension sees. Traceless in ``M_P``, no local term. Lengths are taken in units of the outer radius, so the primitives are of order one; float64, broadcast over leading axes. |  | ✓ |
| `annulus_mean_log` | The area average of ``ln(b/r)`` over the annulus ``a < r < b``: ``1/2 - a^2 ln(b/a) / (b^2 - a^2)``. |  |  |
| `segment_field` | ``B`` at ``points`` from a straight current segment running ``a -> b``, in tesla. |  |  |
